Function: Used to check the configuration after generation
Author: Nguyen Quan (user)

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha version register. Reports the IP major and minor version numbers.

Bits.Description:
Major version number of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 IP. Software reads it to select a compatible driver.

Usage: Read after reset and before any other register; software never writes this field.

Values:
0x1 major version 1 (reset value).

Unit: none

Limits: 16-bit unsigned value.

Minor version number of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 IP. Software reads it to identify compatible additions.

Usage: Read after reset and before any other register; software never writes this field.

Values:
0x0 minor version 0 (reset value).

Unit: none

Limits: 16-bit unsigned value.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha control register. Enables the engine and starts, directs and aborts one message.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Key slot. Index that the engine presents to the key store with the key request when a message starts.

Usage: Program before start; do not change while busy. The key store decides which key belongs to the slot.

Values:
0x0 to 0xF key store slot index (reset value 0x0).

Unit: none

Limits: Four-bit value.

DMA tail mode. Selects how the last, shorter burst of a message is requested from the system DMA controller.

Usage: Program before start together with the watermark fields; used only when dma_en is set.

Values:
0x0 short burst of the exact number of remaining beats (reset value);
0x1 single-beat transfers for the remaining beats.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

DMA request enable. Lets the engine drive the write and read request outputs of the system DMA controller handshake.

Usage: Set before start when a DMA controller moves the data; leave clear for polling or interrupt use. Effective only when the build parameter PARA_DMA_EN is 1.

Values:
0x0 both request outputs held low (reset value);
0x1 request outputs follow the burst rules.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Message abort. Writing one stops the message in progress, discards the data held in the window FIFOs and returns the engine to idle.

Usage: Write one only while busy is set; hardware clears the bit when the engine is idle and the FIFOs are empty. The tag check of an aborted message is not performed and no done event is raised.

Values:
0x0 no abort requested (reset value);
0x1 abort the current message.

Unit: none

Limits: Self-clearing by hardware.

Direction. Selects encryption, which produces ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag, or decryption, which consumes ciphertext followed by the tag and checks it.

Usage: Program before start; do not change while busy.

Values:
0x0 encrypt (reset value);
0x1 decrypt.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Message start. Writing one asks the engine to latch the message parameters and begin one AEAD operation.

Usage: Write one after en, dir, aad_len, msg_len, the watermark fields and the nonce or counter registers are programmed. Hardware clears the bit when it has latched the parameters, so a read of zero means the start was accepted; a write while busy is ignored.

Values:
0x0 no start requested (reset value);
0x1 start one message.

Unit: none

Limits: Self-clearing by hardware; a hardware load in the cycle of a software write has no effect, so software writes start once and polls it.

Engine enable. Allows the engine to accept a message; while it is clear the engine stays idle and its core clock may be gated.

Usage: Set before writing start; clear only while the busy status bit is clear. Software writes it; hardware never changes it.

Values:
0x0 engine disabled (reset value);
0x1 engine enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha length register. Gives the associated data length and the message data length of one message.

Bits.Description:
Message data length. Number of bytes of plaintext or ciphertext, not counting the 16-byte tag.

Usage: Program before start; do not change while busy. A value above the build parameter PARA_MSG_MAX_B sets the len_err event and the message is not started.

Values:
0x0 empty message (reset value);
0x1 to 0xFFFF number of message data bytes.

Unit: byte

Limits: 0 to 65535 bytes, and not above PARA_MSG_MAX_B.

Associated data length. Number of bytes of additional authenticated data that precede the message data in the input stream.

Usage: Program before start; do not change while busy. The engine counts this many bytes of the input stream as associated data and pads them to a multiple of 16 bytes for Poly1305 itself.

Values:
0x0 no associated data (reset value);
0x1 to 0xFFFF number of associated data bytes.

Unit: byte

Limits: 0 to 65535 bytes.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha watermark register. Sets the burst length that the DMA request outputs ask for.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Read watermark. Number of data-width beats that one read request of the DMA channel asks the system DMA controller to read from the output window.

Usage: Program before start when dma_en is set. The IP raises the read request only when that many beats are available in the output FIFO.

Values:
0x1 to 0x100 burst length in beats (reset value 0x1).

Unit: beat of PARA_AXI_DW bits

Limits: 1 to the smaller of the longest INCR burst that fits in 4 KB and the output FIFO depth; a larger value sets the len_err event.

This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Write watermark. Number of data-width beats that one write request of the DMA channel asks the system DMA controller to write into the input window.

Usage: Program before start when dma_en is set. The IP raises the write request only when the input FIFO has room for the requested beats.

Values:
0x1 to 0x100 burst length in beats (reset value 0x1).

Unit: beat of PARA_AXI_DW bits

Limits: 1 to the smaller of the longest INCR burst that fits in 4 KB and the input FIFO depth; a larger value sets the len_err event.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha nonce word 0 register. Holds 32 bits of the 96-bit nonce of RFC 8439.

Bits.Description:
Nonce word 0. The 96-bit nonce is three 32-bit little-endian words; this register is word 0, where word 0 is the least significant.

Usage: Program before start for every decryption, and for every encryption when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 0. The nonce shall be unique for each message under the same key and shall not be generated randomly. Ignored for encryption when PARA_NONCE_HW is 1.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF nonce word 0 (reset value 0x0).

Unit: none

Limits: 32-bit value; do not change while busy.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha nonce word 1 register. Holds 32 bits of the 96-bit nonce of RFC 8439.

Bits.Description:
Nonce word 1. The 96-bit nonce is three 32-bit little-endian words; this register is word 1, where word 0 is the least significant.

Usage: Program before start for every decryption, and for every encryption when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 0. The nonce shall be unique for each message under the same key and shall not be generated randomly. Ignored for encryption when PARA_NONCE_HW is 1.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF nonce word 1 (reset value 0x0).

Unit: none

Limits: 32-bit value; do not change while busy.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha nonce word 2 register. Holds 32 bits of the 96-bit nonce of RFC 8439.

Bits.Description:
Nonce word 2. The 96-bit nonce is three 32-bit little-endian words; this register is word 2, where word 0 is the least significant.

Usage: Program before start for every decryption, and for every encryption when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 0. The nonce shall be unique for each message under the same key and shall not be generated randomly. Ignored for encryption when PARA_NONCE_HW is 1.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF nonce word 2 (reset value 0x0).

Unit: none

Limits: 32-bit value; do not change while busy.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha salt register. Holds the fixed 32-bit part of the hardware-managed nonce.

Bits.Description:
Nonce salt. Upper 32 bits of the 96-bit nonce when the engine manages the nonce itself; the lower 64 bits are the hardware counter.

Usage: Used only for encryption when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 1; program before the first encryption under a key.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF salt value (reset value 0x0).

Unit: none

Limits: 32-bit value; do not change while busy.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha counter low register. Holds the low word of the 64-bit hardware nonce counter.

Bits.Description:
Nonce counter, bits 31 to 0. Software loads the start value and the engine increments the 64-bit counter after each encrypted message.

Usage: Used only when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 1. Write both counter words before the first encryption after reset; the engine refuses to encrypt until a start value has been loaded.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF counter bits 31 to 0 (reset value 0x0).

Unit: message

Limits: 32-bit value; a hardware load in the cycle of a software write has no effect, so write it only while idle.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha counter high register. Holds the high word of the 64-bit hardware nonce counter.

Bits.Description:
Nonce counter, bits 63 to 32. Together with the low word it forms the 64-bit counter that is the lower part of the hardware-managed nonce.

Usage: Used only when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 1. Write both counter words before the first encryption after reset.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF counter bits 63 to 32 (reset value 0x0).

Unit: message

Limits: 32-bit value; write it only while idle.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha status register. Reports the live state of the engine and of its window FIFOs.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Counter valid. Set after software has loaded a start value into the hardware nonce counter since the last reset.

Usage: Meaningful only when the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW is 1; read it to check that encryption is allowed.

Values:
0x0 counter not loaded (reset value);
0x1 counter loaded.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value; stays zero when PARA_NONCE_HW is 0.

Output ready. Set while the output window FIFO holds at least a read-watermark burst, or the last shorter burst of a finished message.

Usage: Poll in polling mode before reading a burst from the data window.

Values:
0x0 no burst available (reset value);
0x1 burst available.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Input ready. Set while the input window FIFO has room for a write-watermark burst.

Usage: Poll in polling mode before writing a burst to the data window.

Values:
0x0 not enough room (reset value);
0x1 room for wm_wr beats.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value; the live value can change between the read and the next write.

Busy. Set from the accepted start until the message is complete or aborted.

Usage: Poll to detect completion when interrupts are not used; configuration registers are not changed while it is set.

Values:
0x0 engine idle (reset value);
0x1 message in progress.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha raw interrupt register. Holds the raw event bits before masking.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Key store error event, raw. Set by hardware when the key store answered a key request with an error (empty or locked slot).

Usage: Software writes one to clear the event after servicing it. A new event in the same cycle as a clear is kept.

Values:
0x0 no event (reset value);
0x1 event pending.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Nonce counter error event, raw. Set by hardware when an encryption was started in hardware nonce mode while the counter was not loaded or the counter would wrap, or, with the nonce check built in, a software nonce equals the previous encryption nonce on the same key slot.

Usage: Software writes one to clear the event after servicing it. A new event in the same cycle as a clear is kept.

Values:
0x0 no event (reset value);
0x1 event pending.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Data window error event, raw. Set by hardware when the data window answered SLVERR for an underrun, an overrun, an unsupported burst or a non-secure access, or the AXI domain was reset while a message ran.

Usage: Software writes one to clear the event after servicing it. A new event in the same cycle as a clear is kept.

Values:
0x0 no event (reset value);
0x1 event pending.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Length or watermark error event, raw. Set by hardware when a length register above the allowed limit or a watermark above the allowed maximum was programmed at start.

Usage: Software writes one to clear the event after servicing it. A new event in the same cycle as a clear is kept.

Values:
0x0 no event (reset value);
0x1 event pending.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Tag error event, raw. Set by hardware when a decryption finished and the received tag did not match the computed tag.

Usage: Software writes one to clear the event after servicing it. A new event in the same cycle as a clear is kept.

Values:
0x0 no event (reset value);
0x1 event pending.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Message done event, raw. Set by hardware when the engine finished a message and, for a decryption, the tag matched.

Usage: Software writes one to clear the event after servicing it. A new event in the same cycle as a clear is kept.

Values:
0x0 no event (reset value);
0x1 event pending.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha interrupt enable register. Selects which events reach the interrupt output.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Key store error interrupt enable. Lets the raw key_err event reach the interrupt output.

Usage: Program before start; may be changed at any time.

Values:
0x0 event masked (reset value);
0x1 event enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Nonce counter error interrupt enable. Lets the raw ctr_err event reach the interrupt output.

Usage: Program before start; may be changed at any time.

Values:
0x0 event masked (reset value);
0x1 event enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Data window error interrupt enable. Lets the raw axi_err event reach the interrupt output.

Usage: Program before start; may be changed at any time.

Values:
0x0 event masked (reset value);
0x1 event enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Length or watermark error interrupt enable. Lets the raw len_err event reach the interrupt output.

Usage: Program before start; may be changed at any time.

Values:
0x0 event masked (reset value);
0x1 event enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Tag error interrupt enable. Lets the raw tag_err event reach the interrupt output.

Usage: Program before start; may be changed at any time.

Values:
0x0 event masked (reset value);
0x1 event enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Message done interrupt enable. Lets the raw done event reach the interrupt output.

Usage: Program before start; may be changed at any time.

Values:
0x0 event masked (reset value);
0x1 event enabled.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha interrupt injection register. Raises raw events from software for testing.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

Key store error event injection. A rising edge of this bit raises the raw key_err event, for software testing of the interrupt path.

Usage: Write zero and then one to inject; used in bring-up and driver tests only.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject the event.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Nonce counter error event injection. A rising edge of this bit raises the raw ctr_err event, for software testing of the interrupt path.

Usage: Write zero and then one to inject; used in bring-up and driver tests only.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject the event.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Data window error event injection. A rising edge of this bit raises the raw axi_err event, for software testing of the interrupt path.

Usage: Write zero and then one to inject; used in bring-up and driver tests only.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject the event.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Length or watermark error event injection. A rising edge of this bit raises the raw len_err event, for software testing of the interrupt path.

Usage: Write zero and then one to inject; used in bring-up and driver tests only.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject the event.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Tag error event injection. A rising edge of this bit raises the raw tag_err event, for software testing of the interrupt path.

Usage: Write zero and then one to inject; used in bring-up and driver tests only.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject the event.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Message done event injection. A rising edge of this bit raises the raw done event, for software testing of the interrupt path.

Usage: Write zero and then one to inject; used in bring-up and driver tests only.

Values:
0x0 no injection (reset value);
0x1 inject the event.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit value.

Table - Register Definition.Description: ChaCha capability register. Reports the build configuration of the IP to the driver.

Bits.Description:
This field is unused.
Read-as-zero and write-ignored.

DMA build option. Reflects the build parameter PARA_DMA_EN.

Usage: Read once at initialisation to learn whether the DMA request outputs exist.

Values:
0x0 no DMA request logic (reset value);
0x1 DMA request outputs present.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit constant.

Tag-hold build option. Reflects the build parameter PARA_HOLD_EN.

Usage: Read once at initialisation: when set, decrypted data is released only after the tag is verified.

Values:
0x0 decrypted data released as produced (reset value);
0x1 decrypted data held until the tag is verified.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit constant.

Hardware nonce build option. Reflects the build parameter PARA_NONCE_HW.

Usage: Read once at initialisation to choose how the driver supplies the nonce.

Values:
0x0 nonce supplied by software (reset value);
0x1 hardware-managed nonce counter.

Unit: none

Limits: One-bit constant.
